fact: Many decisions arise via the accumulation of noisy evidence to a threshold or bound.
source_span: Many decisions are thought to arise via the accumulation of noisy evidence to a threshold or bound . In the model , noisy momentary evidence is accumulated until the integral of the evidence ( termed the decision variable , DV ) reaches one of two bounds at 簣B ( t ) , or until the motion stimulus is terminated by the experimenter .
abstract_sentence: Many decisions arise via the accumulation of noisy evidence to a threshold or bound.

fact: In perception, the mechanism explains the effect of stimulus strength, characterized by signal-to-noise ratio, on decision speed, accuracy and confidence.
source_span: In perception , the mechanism explains the effect of stimulus strength , characterized by signal-to-noise ratio , on decision speed , accuracy and confidence . The noisiness of the momentary evidence causes the DV to wander from its starting point ... Noise is the main determinant of both RT and confidence when signal-to-noise is low , that is when choices are more stochastic ( less accurate ) .
abstract_sentence: In perception, the accumulation of noisy evidence explains how stimulus strength affects decision speed, accuracy, and confidence.

fact: An increase in noise should lead to faster decisions , reduced accuracy and , paradoxically , higher confidence .
source_span: An increase in noise should lead to faster decisions , reduced accuracy and , paradoxically , higher confidence . Specifically , were it possible to leave unchanged the expectation of each sample of momentary evidence while boosting the noise associated with it , then the bounded accumulation of the noisier samples should lead to ( i ) lower accuracy when the expectation of the momentary evidence is strong , ( ii ) faster reaction times when the momentary evidence is weak , and ( iii ) increased confidence when the momentary evidence is weak . The important point is that by increasing noise , the volatility manipulation accelerates the dispersion of the decision variable away from its expected value and nearer the termination bounds , hence faster RT. Increased volatility should affect confidence because it mimics an increase in the diffusion rate ... its main effect on the DV is to accelerate its exodus away from neutral ( probability correct = 0 . 5 ) to more extreme values . Therefore , we predicted that volatility would increase confidence at low coherences.
abstract_sentence: An increase in noise should lead to faster decisions, reduced accuracy, and paradoxically, higher confidence according to bounded evidence accumulation models.

fact: We introduce a novel sensory manipulation that mimics the addition of unbiased noise to motion-selective regions of visual cortex, verified with neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST.
source_span: To test these predictions , we introduce a novel sensory manipulation that mimics the addition of unbiased noise to motion-selective regions of visual cortex , which we verified with neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST . which we verified with neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST . We therefore sought a method to manipulate the variance associated with the neural representation of momentary evidence without affecting its mean. We achieved this with a manipulation of the motion information in a random dot motion (RDM) display, by adding a second level of randomness which increased its volatility but was unbiased with respect to the strength and direction of motion evidence. We verified that the manipulation has the desired properties by recording from direction selective neurons in the middle temporal (MT) and medial superior temporal (MST) areas of the macaque visual cortex. Neurons in these areas are known to represent the momentary evidence in tasks identical to those in our study.
abstract_sentence: The study introduced a novel sensory manipulation that mimics adding unbiased noise to motion-selective regions of visual cortex, verified by neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST.

fact: For both humans and monkeys , increasing the noise induced faster decisions and greater confidence over a range of stimuli for which accuracy was minimally impaired .
source_span: For both humans and monkeys , increasing the noise induced faster decisions and greater confidence over a range of stimuli for which accuracy was minimally impaired . The main effect of high volatility was to decrease RTs , particularly at the weakest motion strengths ( Figure 3B , bottom row , red ) . This effect was robust for all three human subjects and the monkey ( Equation 16 , all p<0 . 03 , t-test , H0: 帣2=0 ) . The proportion of trials the monkey decided to waive the sure-bet option (deciding instead for a riskier direction choice) was greater on the high volatility trials... Thus, high volatility increased the monkey’s confidence, and did so despite a negligible effect on accuracy. The results from the human observers were similar to those from the monkey... They also reported higher confidence for the high volatility stimuli, and the effect was most apparent for the low coherence stimuli... Volatility again did not affect accuracy systematically.
abstract_sentence: For both humans and monkeys, increasing noise induced faster decisions and greater confidence over a range of stimuli with minimal impairment to accuracy.

fact: The magnitude of the effects was in agreement with predictions of a bounded evidence accumulation model .
source_span: The magnitude of the effects was in agreement with predictions of a bounded evidence accumulation model . The family of bounded evidence accumulation models ... depicts the decision process as a race between competing accumulators ... The decision terminates when the accumulated evidence for one alternative ... reaches a threshold or bound , thereby determining both the choice and the decision time . Confidence in the decision derives from a mapping between the DV and the probability that a decision based on this DV will be correct . Solid traces are fits of a bounded evidence accumulation ( drift diffusion ) model ... where the variance of the momentary evidence is the only parameter that we allowed to change between conditions of high and low volatility. The overall quality of the fits?cross all tasks and both species?ndicates that the influence of motion strength and volatility on choice , reaction time and confidence can be explained by a common mechanism of bounded evidence accumulation .
abstract_sentence: The magnitude of the effects of noise on decision speed and confidence matched predictions of a bounded evidence accumulation model.

fact: The deamidase OspI from enteric bacteria Shigella flexneri deamidates a glutamine residue in the host ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme UBC13 and converts it to glutamate ( Q100E ) .
source_span: The deamidase OspI from enteric bacteria Shigella flexneri deamidates a glutamine residue in the host ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme UBC13 and converts it to glutamate ( Q100E ) .
abstract_sentence: The deamidase OspI from Shigella flexneri converts glutamine 100 in UBC13 to glutamate.

fact: The deamidase OspI from Shigella flexneri modifies a glutamine residue (Q100) in the host enzyme UBC13 to glutamate, inhibiting its polyubiquitination activity and downstream NF-κB inflammatory response.
source_span: The deamidase OspI from enteric bacteria Shigella flexneri deamidates a glutamine residue in the host ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme UBC13 and converts it to glutamate ( Q100E ) . Consequently , its polyubiquitination activity in complex with the RING-finger ubiquitin ligase TRAF6 and the downstream NF-庥B inflammatory response is silenced . The Shigella flexneri effector OspI suppresses the inflammatory response (NF-κB pathway) via deamidation of UBC13 at Q100. By an unknown mechanism, deamidation of Q100 to E100 inhibits the synthesis of K63-linked polyubiquitin chains by the UBC13/TRAF6 complex, preventing the downstream activation of NF-κB pathway. The human pathogenic bacteria Shigella flexneri inactivates the host inflammatory Nf-庥B signaling , responsible for inducing inflammatory cytokine responses during pathogen invasion ( Sanada et al . , 2012 ) . To inactivate Nf-庥B signaling , Shigella flexneri secretes a Type III effector called OspI , which functions as a deamidase ( Sanada et al . , 2012 ) . In the early events of interleukin-dependent activation of Nf-庥B signaling , the Ub-conjugating enzyme UBC13 , and the Ub-ligase TRAF6 function together to synthesize both unanchored polyubiquitin chains , and anchored polyubiquitin chains on TRAF6 and its substrate NEMO ( Chen , 2005 ) . These chains serve as a scaffold to bring together TAK1/2 and IKK kinases , eventually leading to phosphorylation and activation of the IKK kinases , I庥B degradation and nuclear translocation of transcription factor Nf-庥B .
abstract_sentence: Deamidation of UBC13 by OspI inhibits its polyubiquitination activity with TRAF6 and silences the downstream NF-κB inflammatory response.

fact: Deamidation inhibits the interaction between UBC13 and TRAF6 RING-domain ( TRAF6RING ) by perturbing both the native and transient interactions .
source_span: We report that deamidation inhibits the interaction between UBC13 and TRAF6 RING-domain ( TRAF6RING ) by perturbing both the native and transient interactions . We report that deamidation weakens the non-covalent interaction of UBC13 with RING-finger domain of TRAF6 ( TRAF6RING ) , without perturbing UBC13 structure or the intrinsic enzymatic activity of UBC13 . Altogether, deamidation inhibited the binding of TRAF6RING to UBC13, but neither changed the fold of UBC13 nor its intrinsic E2 activity. We report that deamidation neither alters the fold nor the enzymatic activity of UBC13. NMR and kinetics studies indicate that deamidation does not alter the active site of UBC13. Instead, it reduces the interaction between UBC13 and RING domains to diminish the catalytic effect of the RING.
abstract_sentence: Deamidation inhibits the interaction between UBC13 and the TRAF6 RING domain by disrupting both native and transient protein-protein interactions without altering UBC13's structure or enzymatic activity.

fact: Deamidation creates a new intramolecular salt-bridge in UBC13 that competes with a critical intermolecular salt-bridge at the native UBC13/TRAF6RING interface .
source_span: Deamidation creates a new intramolecular salt-bridge in UBC13 that competes with a critical intermolecular salt-bridge at the native UBC13/TRAF6RING interface . Further studies showed that deamidation disrupts the interaction between UBC13 and TRAF6RING by three mechanisms: i ) A new intramolecular R14/E100 salt-bridge appears in dUBC13 , which competes with a critical intermolecular salt-bridge in the native complex , ii ) the salt-bridge competition also perturbs the UBC13/TRAF6RING transient complexes to inhibit association , and iii ) transient repulsion between the negatively charged E100 and the negatively charged interface of TRAF6RING reduces association between UBC13 and TRAF6RING . Interestingly, an intramolecular salt-bridge was observed between R14 and E100 in dUBC13... At the interface of UBC13/TRAF6RING, R14 of UBC13 forms an intermolecular salt-bridge with E69 of TRAF6RING. The deamidation-induced intramolecular R14/E100 salt-bridge may interfere with the intermolecular R14/E69 salt-bridge to destabilize the complex. The occupancy of the R14/E69 intermolecular salt-bridge dropped from 99% in the wt complex to 40% in the dUBC13 complex ... deamidation reduces the stability of the complex ... the R14/E69 salt-bridge was stable throughout in the wt complex, it disrupted in the dUBC13 complex.
abstract_sentence: Deamidation creates a new intramolecular salt-bridge in UBC13 that competes with a critical intermolecular salt-bridge at the UBC13/TRAF6 interface, weakening their association.

fact: Deamidation reduces the formation and stability of native-like transient complexes and inhibits long-range transient interactions formed by R14 with TRAF6RING.
source_span: The association and stability dropped by 2.3 fold in the dUBC13 complex at low salt, suggesting that deamidation reduces the formation of the native-like transient complex. The new intramolecular salt-bridge also inhibits the long-range transient interactions formed by R14 with TRAF6RING. In the wt complex, a transient attractive interaction was observed between R14 in UBC13 and D57 in TRAF6RING... The R14/D57 interaction was absent in the dUBC13 complex, and it dissociated prematurely. The positions of TRAF6RING are dispersed when it interacts with dUBC13, and none of the clusters coincide with the native complex... Several TRAF6RING clusters around R14 were absent in the dUBC13 complex.
abstract_sentence: Deamidation reduces the formation and stability of native-like transient complexes between UBC13 and TRAF6RING by disrupting long-range transient interactions involving residue R14.

fact: Repulsion between E100 and the negatively charged surface of RING also prevents transient interactions in the UBC13/RING complex .
source_span: Repulsion between E100 and the negatively charged surface of RING also prevents transient interactions in the UBC13/RING complex . Overall, electrostatic repulsion between E100 and the negatively charged interface of TRAF6RING was observed in the dUBC13 transient complexes, which could destabilize it. Overall , titrations studies indicated that all three mechanisms have distinct contributions to the binding between UBC13 and TRAF6RING . ... Given the salt-bridge competition reduces binding energy by 0 . 6 kcal/mol , the repulsive effect of E100 on the transient complex is 0 . 5 kcal/mol . The effect of negatively charged E100 on the transient complex was estimated based on transient complex theory ... any difference between wt and deamidated complex were solely due to transient repulsion between E100 and the acidic residues of TRAF6RING.
abstract_sentence: Electrostatic repulsion between the negatively charged E100 in deamidated UBC13 and the negatively charged surface of TRAF6 RING domain further prevents transient interactions.

fact: Our findings highlight a mechanism wherein a post-translational modification perturbs the conformation and stability of transient complexes to inhibit protein-protein association .
source_span: By a combination of all-atom simulations and experimental data , this study provides molecular details of how PTMs can modulate transient protein-protein association to inhibit interaction . PTMs like phosphorylation , eliminylation , and deamidation can change the surface electrostatics of a protein ( Ribet and Cossart , 2010 ) to modulate the conformation and population of transient complexes significantly . The wt complex was stable throughout the 200 ns trajectory with low rmsd... The deamidated complex was unstable for a significant duration of 75 ns, wherein the rmsd of TRAF6RING increased substantially.
abstract_sentence: Post-translational modification by deamidation perturbs the conformation and stability of transient protein complexes to inhibit protein-protein association.

source_span: Cognitive processes depend on coordinated interactions among large-scale distributed brain networks . Flexible and rapid propagation of information across distant brain regions is necessary to support these functions . ... Frontal and parietal brain regions support WM ( Cohen et al . , 1997; Prabhakaran et al . , 2000; Pessoa et al . , 2002; Todd and Marois , 2004 ) .
abstract_sentence: Working memory depends on coordinated interactions among large-scale brain networks, especially frontal and parietal regions.

fact: Oscillatory synchronization of neuronal activity, especially in the theta frequency range, is hypothesized to enable information exchange within and between brain networks during working memory processes.
source_span: A prominent hypothesis is that information exchange within and between networks occurs through the oscillatory synchronization of neuronal activity , such that synchronous neuronal firing binds neurons into ensembles engaged in specific computational functions ... Oscillatory activity in the theta range ( 4?? Hz ) appears to organize local neuronal ensembles across distant regions during WM processes ...
abstract_sentence: Oscillatory synchronization, especially in the theta frequency range, is hypothesized to enable coordination within and between brain networks during working memory.

fact: Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) was applied at theta frequency (6 Hz) to the right middle frontal gyrus and inferior parietal lobule to modulate frontoparietal network synchronization during working memory tasks.
source_span: In- and anti-phase theta frequency ( 6 Hz ) stimulation was applied across two key nodes of the right frontoparietal network: the middle frontal gyrus and inferior parietal lobule . Theta ( 6 Hz ) tACS was applied to the middle frontal gyrus and inferior parietal lobule nodes ( center electrode locations at F4 and P4 ) of the frontoparietal network in synchronous ( 0簞 relative phase ) and desynchronous ( 180簞 relative phase ) conditions Ten healthy volunteers performed a session of each tACS condition ( synchronous , desynchronous and sham ) in a pseudo-randomized single-blinded cross-over design . Participants performed the Choice Reaction Task ( CRT ) and 1-back and 2-back versions of the N-back task .
abstract_sentence: Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) was applied at theta frequency to the right frontoparietal network to modulate oscillatory synchronization during working memory tasks.

fact: Synchronous (in-phase) tACS stimulation improved working memory performance when cognitive demands were high.
source_span: Externally induced synchronization improved performance when cognitive demands were high . ... We found that synchronous ( in-phase ) stimulation caused an improvement in performance ... Synchronous tACS improved reaction times ( RTs ) for the more demanding 2-back condition compared both to desynchronous tACS and sham . Remarkably, synchronous tACS produced sufficient improvement in response times to make 2-back performance similar to the 1-back condition, which is typically associated with much faster responses. Our observations that tACS had no effect on less demanding 1-back or CRT tasks suggests that the behavioral effects of entraining oscillations interacts with the extent that a network is already engaged by a cognitive task.
abstract_sentence: Synchronous tACS improved working memory performance when cognitive demands were high.

fact: External manipulations of oscillatory synchrony across a right-sided frontoparietal network impact neural activity and modify behavior. The effects depend on the relative phase of the external oscillators and also the underlying cognitive state at the time tACS is applied.
source_span: In Experiment 2 we use simultaneous tACS-fMRI to investigate the neural correlates of the phase dependent effects of tACS. Our results demonstrate that external manipulations of oscillatory synchrony across a right-sided frontoparietal network impact neural activity and modify behavior. The effects depend on the relative phase of the external oscillators and also the underlying cognitive state at the time tACS is applied. Our imaging results for the 2-back and CRT tasks strongly support these notions and show how the physiological effect of external oscillatory manipulations are highly dependent on the underlying cognitive state. While synchronous and desynchronous stimulation produced distinct activity and connectivity patterns in the 2-back task, they resulted in similar changes of activity and no effects on connectivity for the CRT task. While synchronous and desynchronous stimulation produced distinct activity and connectivity patterns in the 2-back task, they resulted in similar changes of activity and no effects on connectivity for the CRT task.
abstract_sentence: Simultaneous tACS-fMRI shows that tACS effects on brain activity depend on the relative phase of stimulation and the cognitive state during working memory tasks.

fact: Synchronous tACS during the verbal WM task increased parietal activity, which correlated with behavioral performance.
source_span: Specifically , synchronous tACS during the verbal WM task increased parietal activity , which correlated with behavioral performance . We show that increased activity within the right inferior parietal lobe correlated with faster responses during the 2-back, supporting a link between neural activity and the behavioral effects of tACS. Entraining synchronous activity across the right frontoparietal network was associated with increased activity within the inferior parietal lobe and middle frontal gyrus, regions known to play a key role in WM function.
abstract_sentence: Synchronous tACS during a verbal working memory task increased parietal brain activity, which correlated with better behavioral performance.

During synchronous stimulation, functional connectivity increased between the IPL-electrode region and frontal parts of the frontoparietal network, that is, DLPFC. While synchronous stimulation resulted in increased functional connectivity between parietal and frontal areas
abstract_sentence: The relative phase of frontoparietal tACS stimulation influences functional connectivity and information flow within the working memory network.

fact: The study found a direct link between behavioral performance in a demanding working-memory task and large-scale brain synchronization across a right frontoparietal network activated by the task.
source_span: Overall, our findings indicate a direct link between behavioral performance in a demanding working-memory task and large-scale brain synchronization across a right frontoparietal network activated by the task.
abstract_sentence: There is a direct link between behavioral performance in demanding working memory tasks and large-scale brain synchronization across a right frontoparietal network.

fact: The granular retrosplenial cortex (RSG) is critical for both spatial and non-spatial behaviors.
source_span: The granular retrosplenial cortex ( RSG ) is critical for both spatial and non-spatial behaviors , but the underlying neural codes remain poorly understood .
abstract_sentence: The granular retrosplenial cortex (RSG) is critical for both spatial and non-spatial behaviors.

fact: Channelrhodopsin-assisted circuit mapping (CRACM) was used to study subtype-specific circuits formed by anterior thalamic, claustral, anterior cingulate, and dorsal subicular inputs to the RSG.
source_span: Here , we use channelrhodopsin ( ChR2 ) -assisted circuit mapping ( CRACM ) to study the subtype-specific circuits formed by anterior thalamic , claustral , anterior cingulate , and dorsal subicular inputs to the RSG .
abstract_sentence: Optogenetic circuit mapping in mice reveals parallel circuits in superficial RSG that process different inputs.

fact: The anterior thalamus and dorsal subiculum, sources of spatial information, strongly and selectively recruit small low-rheobase (LR) pyramidal cells in RSG.
source_span: The anterior thalamus and dorsal subiculum , sources of spatial information , strongly and selectively recruit small low-rheobase ( LR ) pyramidal cells in RSG . Specifically , we find that anterior thalamus and dorsal subiculum preferentially control LR neurons , whereas claustrum and anterior cingulate control RS cells . From resting membrane potentials ... LR neurons were strongly driven past spike threshold by these thalamic inputs while RS neurons exhibited far smaller EPSPs ... this stimulation evoked a significant increase in spiking in LR neurons ... but not RS neurons ... LR neurons thus had a significantly larger increase in spike rate evoked by the optical pulse than RS neurons. our functional findings that LR neurons are preferentially driven by both ADAV and DS inputs , while RS neurons are targeted by CLA and ACC inputs .
abstract_sentence: Anterior thalamus and dorsal subiculum inputs selectively recruit low-rheobase (LR) pyramidal neurons in superficial RSG.

fact: Claustral and anterior cingulate inputs, sources of mostly non-spatial information, preferentially control neighboring regular-spiking (RS) cells in RSG.
source_span: In contrast , neighboring regular-spiking ( RS ) cells are preferentially controlled by claustral and anterior cingulate inputs , sources of mostly non-spatial information . Dendritic lamination plots of LR and RS dendrites and projection density plots of CLA axons and terminal arbors show that RS , but not LR , apical dendrites anatomically overlap with CLA arbors in superficial layers 1 c and two and upper layer 5 . Thus , both claustrocortical and corticocortical inputs to RSG target RS apical dendrites at the lower divisions of L1 ( L1c and L1b/c , respectively ) RS cells have significantly larger EPSP amplitudes compared to LR cells ... reflecting the precise overlap of ACC arbors and RS dendrites ... LR EPSP amplitudes across all layers were much lower in magnitude
abstract_sentence: Neighboring regular-spiking (RS) pyramidal neurons in superficial RSG are preferentially controlled by claustral and anterior cingulate inputs, which carry mostly non-spatial information.

fact: Precise sublaminar axonal and dendritic arborization within RSG layer 1 permits this parallel processing.
source_span: Precise sublaminar axonal and dendritic arborization within RSG layer 1 , in particular , permits this parallel processing . Our results reveal a double dissociation in the precise organization of afferent axons and principal cell dendrites that can support parallel processing in superficial RSG . This again indicates that parallel circuits in RSG process TC versus ClaC and CC information , and this parallel processing is enabled by precise sublaminar organization of afferent axons and layer three principal cell apical dendrites In summary , our results highlight a superficial retrosplenial circuit enabled by the precise sublaminar organization of distinct principal neuronal subtypes and axonal afferents .
abstract_sentence: Precise sublaminar axonal and dendritic arborization within RSG layer 1 enables parallel processing of spatial and non-spatial inputs by distinct neuron subtypes.

fact: Observed thalamocortical synaptic dynamics enable computational models of LR neurons to compute the speed of head rotation, despite receiving head direction inputs that do not explicitly encode speed.
source_span: Observed thalamocortical synaptic dynamics enable computational models of LR neurons to compute the speed of head rotation , despite receiving head direction inputs that do not explicitly encode speed . We show that the synaptic dynamics of thalamic inputs allow for the robust encoding of angular speed by LR cell models , even though these inputs only explicitly contain information about head direction , not speed . Taken together , these results suggest that synaptic depression of HD ensemble inputs introduces an angular head speed signal into the LR population , producing neurons that are more responsive during faster head turns ... Both the simulations and the analytical theory show that synaptic depression of HD cell input onto LR cells should result in angular speed coding in the LR cell firing rate , and that anticipatory firing improves both the precision and quality of this coding .
abstract_sentence: Thalamocortical synaptic dynamics enable LR neurons in RSG to compute angular head speed from head direction inputs that do not explicitly encode speed.

fact: Parallel input streams identify a distinct principal neuronal subtype ideally positioned to support spatial orientation computations in the RSG.
source_span: Thus , parallel input streams identify a distinct principal neuronal subtype ideally positioned to support spatial orientation computations in the RSG . abstract_sentence: Parallel input streams identify LR pyramidal neurons as a distinct principal neuronal subtype ideally positioned to support spatial orientation computations in RSG.

fact: A stable number of petals helps ensure reliable flower opening and pollinator attraction, supporting reproductive success.
source_span: Petals are usually required to open the flower and to help attract pollinators… therefore a stable number of petals could ensure a reliable display of the reproductive organs and a reproducible cue for pollinators.
abstract_sentence: Stable floral forms support reproductive success by ensuring reliable flower opening and pollinator attraction.

fact: The flowers of A. thaliana and other Brassicaceae species are readily distinguished by their four petals. This phenotype is robust to natural genetic variation; for example, flowers from genetically diverse A. thaliana accessions consistently produce four petals.
source_span: The flowers of A . thaliana and other Brassicaceae species are readily distinguished by their four petals . This phenotype is robust to natural genetic variation; for example , flowers from genetically diverse A . thaliana accessions consistently produce four petals ( Figure 1a ) .
abstract_sentence: Petal number is a robust trait in Arabidopsis thaliana flowers, consistently producing four petals across genetically diverse plants.

fact: Petal number, for example, is invariant in Arabidopsis thaliana flowers. However, petal number varies in the closely related species Cardamine hirsuta.
source_span: Petal number, for example, is invariant in Arabidopsis thaliana flowers. However, petal number varies in the closely related species Cardamine hirsuta, and the genetic basis for this difference between species is unknown. Cardamine hirsuta flowers display a variable number of petals, between zero and four, on a single plant… This phenotype varies in response to both environmental and genetic perturbation. C . hirsuta lacks this robustness and shows variation in petal number . For example , we found similar frequencies of each petal number between zero and four in flowers from 39 C . hirsuta accessions sampled from across the species range ( Figure 1b ) ( Hay et al . , 2014 ) . Therefore , petal number varies within C . hirsuta and is a species-level trait that distinguishes C . hirsuta from A . thaliana .
abstract_sentence: Petal number varies in the closely related species Cardamine hirsuta, unlike the invariant petal number in Arabidopsis thaliana.

fact: Divergence in the pleiotropic floral regulator APETALA1 (AP1) can account for the species-specific difference in petal number robustness.
source_span: Here we show that divergence in the pleiotropic floral regulator APETALA1 (AP1) can account for the species-specific difference in petal number robustness. In this study , we investigate the evolutionary transition from a robust phenotype of four petals , typified by A . thaliana , to a variable petal number in C . hirsuta . We show that divergence in the pleiotropic floral regulator AP1 can account for the difference in petal number robustness between species . In this study , we identified AP1 as a gene of major effect in the evolutionary transition from a robust phenotype of four petals , typified by A . thaliana , to a variable petal number in C . hirsuta . AP1 is an important regulator of A . thaliana flower development , acting early to initiate flowers and later to specify floral organs ( Bowman et al . , 1993; Irish and Sussex , 1990; Mandel et al . , 1992 ) .
abstract_sentence: Divergence in the floral regulator gene APETALA1 (AP1) explains the species-specific difference in petal number robustness between Arabidopsis thaliana and Cardamine hirsuta.

fact: A. thaliana AP1 confers robustness by masking the phenotypic expression of quantitative trait loci controlling petal number in C. hirsuta.
source_span: This large effect of AP1 is explained by epistatic interactions: A. thaliana AP1 confers robustness by masking the phenotypic expression of quantitative trait loci controlling petal number in C. hirsuta. This large effect of AP1 is explained by epistatic interactions: A . thaliana AP1 masks the phenotypic expression of all petal number QTL in C . hirsuta and , in this way , confers robustness . this transgene was sufficient to convert C . hirsuta petal number from variable to robust , elevating petal number towards the A . thaliana value of four petals the allelic effects of these 9 QTL were undetectable in the presence of the A . thaliana AP1 genomic locus ... Thus , A . thaliana AP1 canalized C . hirsuta petal number by masking the phenotypic effects of at least 9 QTL .
abstract_sentence: Arabidopsis thaliana AP1 confers robustness in petal number by masking the effects of multiple quantitative trait loci controlling petal number in Cardamine hirsuta.

fact: C. hirsuta AP1 fails to complement this function of A. thaliana AP1, conferring variable petal number, and upstream regulatory regions of AP1 contribute to this divergence.
source_span: We show that C. hirsuta AP1 fails to complement this function of A. thaliana AP1, conferring variable petal number. …and that upstream regulatory regions of AP1 contribute to this divergence. We show that C . hirsuta AP1 fails to complement this function of A . thaliana AP1 , conferring variable petal number , and that upstream regulatory regions of AP1 contribute to this divergence . Therefore, the results of these gene swaps indicate that C. hirsuta AP1 has a reduced ability to promote four petals when compared to A. thaliana AP1.
abstract_sentence: Cardamine hirsuta AP1 fails to complement the robustness function of Arabidopsis thaliana AP1, resulting in variable petal number; upstream regulatory regions contribute to this divergence.

fact: Variable petal number is maintained in C. hirsuta despite sufficient standing genetic variation in natural accessions to produce plants with four-petalled flowers.
source_span: A striking feature of this distribution is the absence of natural accessions with four petals... abstract_sentence: Variable petal number is maintained in Cardamine hirsuta despite sufficient genetic variation in natural accessions to produce four-petalled flowers.

fact: Marburg virus, Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV), and Dengue virus activate and benefit from expression of the transcription regulator nuclear erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2), whereas Nrf2 mobilization counters HIV infection in macrophages.

SFN is a powerful mobilizer of the transcription factor nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 ( Nrf2 ) [22??4] . Nrf2 , a master regulator of the antioxidant response [25 , 26] , ...

fact: SFN blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but not in primary T cells.
source_span: Here we show for the first time that SFN blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but not in primary T cells . Here , unlike in primary T cell cultures , luciferase activity dropped sharply in cultures treated with 10 弮M SFN and fell to background levels with higher SFN concentrations ( Fig 1B ) . Thus , SFN acts to block single-round HIV-1 infections in primary hMDMs but not in primary T cells . Thus, SFN acts to block single-round HIV-1 infections in primary hMDMs but not in primary T cells. Further investigation will be required to determine why SFN fails to block infection in T cells , whether the same pathway could be exploited there as well or whether the restriction can be activated directly by other means .
abstract_sentence: SFN blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but not in primary T cells.

fact: SFN blocks HIV infection in PMA-differentiated promonocytic cell lines but not in other tested cell lines; siRNA-mediated depletion of Nrf2 increases HIV infectivity in primary macrophages and reduces the antiviral effects of SFN treatment.
source_span: Similarly SFN blocks infection in PMA-differentiated promonocytic cell lines , but not in other cell lines tested . siRNA-mediated depletion of Nrf2 boosted HIV infectivity in primary macrophages and reduced the anti-viral effects of SFN treatment . We detected no inhibition of HIV infection after SFN treatment in HeLa, HEK293T or GHOST cells but SFN markedly decreased evidence of infection in U937 and THP1 cultures. In the absence of SFN , depletion of Nrf2 caused a significant increase in luciferase activity indicating that Nrf2 is detrimental to HIV infection in macrophages and that the basal level of Nrf2 that is present in macrophages is sufficient for establishing some anti-viral activity ( Fig 6D ) .
abstract_sentence: SFN blocks HIV infection in certain promonocytic cell lines but not others; Nrf2 depletion increases HIV infectivity and reduces SFN's antiviral effect.

fact: SFN treatment blocks HIV infection after viral entry but before the formation of 2-LTR circles, similar to the antiviral proteins SAMHD1 and MX2.
source_span: We further found that , like the type I interferon-induced cellular anti-viral proteins SAMHD1 and MX2 , SFN treatment blocks infection after entry , but before formation of 2-LTR circles . The vehicle- and SFN-treated samples showed similar levels of late reverse transcription product , indicating that SFN , unlike AZT , did not hinder replication steps from viral entry through reverse transcription ( Fig 7A ) . When we tested for 2-LTR circles ... we found that these were clearly decreased in the AZT and SFN samples relative to the vehicle controls ( Fig 7B ) . Alu-PCR , testing for integrated proviral sequences , also showed that these were similarly decreased in AZT- and SFN-treated cultures ... We found that SFN counters infection whether viral entry is mediated through HIV Env or VSV-G glycoproteins ... This suggests a post-entry block as these glycoproteins engage different entry mechanisms . The fraction of those infected cells closely paralleled the population-wide reporter activity measured with the luciferase reporter virus . This indicates that the SFN-mediated block reduced the number of infected cells rather than suppressing transcription from similar numbers of infected cells .
abstract_sentence: SFN blocks HIV infection after viral entry but before formation of 2-LTR circles, similar to antiviral proteins SAMHD1 and MX2.

fact: SFN does not upregulate the antiviral proteins SAMHD1 or MX2 during its inhibition of HIV infection.
source_span: Interestingly however , neither SAMHD1 nor MX2 were upregulated . We immunoblotted lysates of mock- and SFN-treated U937 cells for SAMHD1 and found that while SAMHD1 was readily detected in THP1 lysates, it remained undetectable in U937 lysates under the conditions tested. This indicates that SFN does not block HIV by increasing SAMHD1 levels. SFN did not significantly change levels of either SAMHD1 or MX2 . Conversely , IFN帢 treatment increased levels of MX2 as expected .
abstract_sentence: SFN does not increase levels of known antiviral proteins SAMHD1 or MX2 during HIV inhibition.

fact: Nrf2 action can potently block HIV infection and highlights a novel way to trigger this inhibition.
source_span: This shows for the first time that Nrf2 action can potently block HIV infection and highlights a novel way to trigger this inhibition .
abstract_sentence: Nrf2 activation can potently block HIV infection, revealing a novel antiviral mechanism.

fact: Aedes-borne arboviruses continue to precipitate epidemics worldwide.
source_span: Aedes-borne arboviruses continue to precipitate epidemics worldwide .
abstract_sentence: Aedes-borne arboviruses such as dengue and Zika continue to cause epidemics worldwide.

fact: In Dominican Republic, the appearance of Zika virus cases that closely followed a large dengue epidemic provided an opportunity to study the different transmission drivers behind these two flaviviruses.
source_span: In Dominican Republic , the appearance of Zika virus cases that closely followed a large dengue epidemic provided an opportunity to study the different transmission drivers behind these two flaviviruses . As this outbreak abated , the first cases of Zika were detected .
abstract_sentence: The Dominican Republic experienced a large dengue epidemic followed closely by Zika virus cases, providing an opportunity to study differences in transmission between these two flaviviruses.

fact: Expectedly, box plots showed that 75% of dengue was reported in those aged <20 years while Zika infections were more widely dispersed among the population.
source_span: Expectedly , box plots showed that 75% of dengue was reported in those aged <20 years while Zika infections were more widely dispersed among the population . Boxplots established the distribution of cases among the population ... and revealed that 75% of all dengue cases occurred before the age of 20 compared with ~42 for Zika.
abstract_sentence: Dengue cases were predominantly reported in individuals under 20 years old, while Zika infections were more evenly distributed across age groups.

fact: Dengue attack rates were marginally higher among males at 25.9 per 10,000 population vs. 21.5 per 10,000 population for females.
source_span: Dengue attack rates were marginally higher among males at 25 . 9 per 10 , 000 population vs . 21 . 5 per 10 , 000 population for females . As a percentage, dengue infections were higher among men than women: 54.5% ... vs. 45.5% ... respectively.
abstract_sentence: Dengue attack rates were slightly higher in males compared to females in the Dominican Republic.

fact: Zika infections appeared to be highly clustered among females (73.8% (95% CI 72.6%, 75.0%; p<0.05)); age-adjusted Zika attack rates among females were 7.64 per 10,000 population compared with 2.72 per 10,000 population among males.
source_span: Zika infections appeared to be highly clustered among females ( 73 . 8% ( 95% CI 72 . 6% , 75 . 0%; p<0 . 05 ) ) ; age-adjusted Zika attack rates among females were 7 . 64 per 10 , 000 population compared with 2 . 72 per 10 , 000 population among males . By comparison, Zika infection was markedly lower among men than women: 26.2% ... vs. 73.8% ... respectively.
abstract_sentence: Zika infections were significantly more common among females, with 73.8% of cases occurring in women.

fact: R0 calculations stratified by sex showed a significantly higher metric among females: 1.84 (1.82, 1.87; p<0.05) compared to males at 1.72 (1.69, 1.75; p<0.05).
source_span: R0 calculations stratified by sex also showed a significantly higher metric among females: 1 . 84 ( 1 . 82 , 1 . 87; p<0 . 05 ) when compared to males at 1 . 72 ( 1 . 69 , 1 . 75; p<0 . 05 ) . Stratifying by sex, the national R0 for males was 1.72 ... and 1.84 ... for females.
abstract_sentence: The basic reproduction number (R0) for Zika was higher in females than males, indicating greater transmission potential among women.

fact: GBS attack rates stratified by sex revealed slightly higher risk in males vs. females, at 0.62 and 0.57 per 10,000 population respectively.
source_span: However , GBS attack rates stratified by sex revealed slightly higher risk in males vs . females , at 0 . 62 and 0 . 57 per 10 , 000 population respectively .
abstract_sentence: Guillain-Barre syndrome attack rates were slightly higher in males than females during the Zika outbreak.

fact: Evidence suggests little impact of existing dengue immunity on reported attack rates of Zika at the population level.
source_span: Evidence suggests little impact of existing dengue immunity on reported attack rates of Zika at the population level . Results indicate that antibody cross-reactivity may not be influencing reported outcomes at the population level.
abstract_sentence: Existing dengue immunity appears to have little impact on the population-level attack rates of Zika virus.

fact: Community awareness campaigns, through influencing short-term health seeking behaviour, remain the most plausible mechanism behind increased reporting among women of reproductive age, although biological susceptibility cannot yet be ruled out.
source_span: The findings indicate that community awareness campaigns , through influencing short-term health seeking behaviour , remain the most plausible mechanism behind increased reporting among women of reproductive age , although biological susceptibility cannot yet be ruled out . Evidence also suggests a greater burden of Zika among women, however this is most likely due to increased health-seeking behaviour rather than biological mechanisms. If correct, targeted advocacy campaigns are effective at changing short-term behaviour and are recommended during Zika epidemics.
abstract_sentence: Community awareness campaigns likely influenced increased reporting of Zika infections among women of reproductive age, though biological susceptibility cannot be excluded.

fact: Media campaigns and screening are therefore recommended for women of reproductive age during Zika outbreaks.
source_span: Media campaigns and screening are therefore recommended for women of reproductive age during Zika outbreaks .
abstract_sentence: Media campaigns and screening are recommended for women of reproductive age during Zika outbreaks to improve detection and response.

fact: Future research should focus on clinical Zika outcomes among dengue seropositive individuals.
source_span: Future research should focus on clinical Zika outcomes among dengue seropositive individuals .
abstract_sentence: Future research should investigate clinical outcomes of Zika infection among individuals previously exposed to dengue virus.

fact: Under nitrogen deprivation, filaments of the cyanobacterium Anabaena develop a one-dimensional pattern of nitrogen-fixing heterocysts separated by about ten photosynthetic vegetative cells.
source_span: Under nitrogen deprivation , filaments of the cyanobacterium Anabaena undergo a process of development , resulting in a one-dimensional pattern of nitrogen-fixing heterocysts separated by about ten photosynthetic vegetative cells .
abstract_sentence: Under nitrogen deprivation, Anabaena filaments develop a one-dimensional pattern of nitrogen-fixing heterocysts separated by about ten vegetative cells.

fact: The transcription factor HetR is essential for heterocyst differentiation in Anabaena, and its expression fluctuations were studied using a chromosomally-encoded translational hetR-gfp fusion.
source_span: We studied the statistics of fluctuations of gene expression of HetR , a transcription factor essential for heterocyst differentiation , both under steady-state growth in nitrogen-rich conditions and at different times following nitrogen deprivation , using a chromosomally-encoded translational hetR-gfp fusion . Our study was conducted using a chromosomal hetR-gfp fusion , thereby avoiding any contribution to fluctuations stemming from cell-cell variability in plasmid copy number , which would preclude accurate evaluation of both noise and cell-cell correlations in expression . As a reporter , a fusion to a fragment of the N-terminal part of the protein was constructed rather than a traditional transcriptional fusion because with the N-terminal translational fusion , expression of the gene with all its transcription and translation start signals is tested . Anabaena sp. strain PCC 7120 and derived mutant strains were used to study hetR expression and heterocyst development under nitrogen-rich and nitrogen-deprived conditions.
abstract_sentence: HetR is a transcription factor essential for heterocyst differentiation, studied using a chromosomally-encoded hetR-gfp fusion in Anabaena.

fact: Statistical analysis shows that hetR expression fluctuations in nearby cells are coupled with a characteristic spatial range of circa two to three cells, defining the scale of cellular interactions along the filament.
source_span: Statistical analysis of fluorescence at the individual cell level in wild-type and mutant filaments demonstrates that expression fluctuations of hetR in nearby cells are coupled , with a characteristic spatial range of circa two to three cells , setting the scale for cellular interactions along a filament . These correlations extend to two to three cells , setting the scale for cellular interactions along a filament . Irrespective of the strain , the behavior illustrated in Fig . 3B and 3C indicates that gene expression between cells under nitrogen-rich conditions is correlated up to distances of two to three cells . The spatial autocorrelation function of hetR-gfp expression along filaments shows that correlations between neighboring cells die out after two to three cells, a range of correlations that is shorter than the characteristic scale of developmental patterns.
abstract_sentence: Expression fluctuations of hetR in neighboring Anabaena cells are coupled with a spatial range of about two to three cells.

fact: Correlations between cells predominantly arise from intercellular molecular transfer and less from cell division.
source_span: Correlations between cells predominantly arise from intercellular molecular transfer and less from cell division . We stress that the dominant part of the observed correlations must derive from intercellular molecular transfer: had the measured correlations been due exclusively to cell division, there would be no difference between the autocorrelation functions pertaining to the different mutant strains. Moreover , we found evidence of the participation of an intercellular communication protein in setting these spatial correlations at specific times during differentiation . Second, the spatial autocorrelation of expression levels as function of the separation between cells decays slower in the ?patS strain than in the WT, showing that the effect of basal PatS expression is to anti-correlate the expression of hetR-gfp between neighboring cells.
abstract_sentence: Correlations in hetR expression between cells mainly arise from intercellular molecular transfer rather than cell division.

fact: Cell-to-cell fluctuations of HetR in Anabaena include essential contributions from the developmental network even when not induced, and fluctuations under nitrogen-rich conditions provide a background for those after nitrogen step-down.
source_span: We conclude that cell-to-cell fluctuations of the master regulator HetR in Anabaena are complex and include essential contributions from the developmental network even when the latter is not induced . To explore the possibility that the fluctuations in gene expression measured under nitrogen-replete conditions provide the background over which cell-to-cell variations build up during the development process, we have carried out an analysis of fluctuations of hetR-gfp expression at different times following nitrogen deprivation. Another manifestation of the correlations between cells is the expression of hetR-gfp in contiguous cells along filaments. Our observations show that these clusters already exist under nitrogen-rich conditions, whereas previous investigations had shown that the differentiation process initiates in small clusters of cells that are later resolved into single heterocysts, after the environmental cue is given [24]. Our measurements of the statistical properties of fluctuations in gene expression of hetR-gfp well after the developmental network has sensed nitrogen step-down, but possibly before a final commitment has been established show that the primordial fluctuations under nitrogen-rich conditions and those at early times after nitrogen step-down, e.g. 3 hours, are statistically similar.
abstract_sentence: Fluctuations in hetR expression under nitrogen-rich conditions provide a background on which developmental fluctuations build after nitrogen deprivation.

fact: Basal steady-state expression of PatS, cell-cell communication influenced by septal protein SepJ, and positive HetR auto-regulation are essential determinants of fluctuations in hetR expression and its distribution along filaments under nitrogen-rich conditions.
source_span: We found that under nitrogen-rich conditions , basal , steady-state expression of the HetR inhibitor PatS , cell-cell communication influenced by the septal protein SepJ and positive HetR auto-regulation are essential determinants of fluctuations in hetR expression and its distribution along filaments . The histograms of the ?patS and ?sepJ mutants are significantly broader than the WT histogram , and their respective means 簣std ( 18簣8 and 19簣7 ) larger than the WT? ( 13簣4 ) . The histogram of ?patS exhibits a particularly long tail of high fluorescence values , which is consistent with a possible lack of inhibition of hetR expression . The histogram corresponding to the ?hetR strain lacking HetR positive auto-regulation is narrower than that of the WT and all the other mutants , and the filaments display fluorescence values that are typically smaller than all other strains . This suggests that autoregulation of hetR is also at play under nitrogen-replete conditions . The cigar shape of the scatter for ?patS ( Pearson coefficient = 0 . 40 ) reveals a larger statistical tendency for nearest neighbors cells to have similar fluorescence than in the WT ( Pearson coefficient = 0 . 25 ) . In contrast , the observed tendency of some highly fluorescent cells to have weakly fluorescent neighbors in ?sepJ filaments ( Pearson coefficient = 0 . 05 ) , suggests that expression fluctuations in this strain are less constrained than in the WT .
abstract_sentence: Under nitrogen-rich conditions, basal PatS expression, cell-cell communication via SepJ, and positive HetR autoregulation determine hetR expression fluctuations and distribution along filaments.

fact: Comparison of hetR-gfp expression under nitrogen-rich and nitrogen-poor conditions highlights differences between HetR inhibitors PatS and HetN, and differences in specificity between septal proteins SepJ and FraC/FraD.
source_span: A comparison between the expression of hetR-gfp under nitrogen-rich and nitrogen-poor conditions highlights the differences between the two HetR inhibitors PatS and HetN , as well as the differences in specificity between the septal proteins SepJ and FraC/FraD . The hetR-gfp fusion was transferred to wild-type Anabaena ( WT ) and mutant strains with deletions in the patS regulatory gene [33] , in the hetN regulatory gene [27] , in the sepJ gene encoding septal protein SepJ [19] , and in the fraC and fraD genes encoding septal proteins FraC and FraD [20] ( see Materials and Methods for details ) . We investigated two mutant strains, ?sepJ and ?fraC/?fraD, both of which lack proteins that are thought to contribute to intercellular septal junction complexes and cell-cell communication. Specifically, we inquired whether the coupling of expression fluctuations of hetR-gfp between neighboring cells is impaired in these mutants. Moreover, the behavior of these mutants, which lack putative septal proteins, differs significantly from both the WT and the mutants ?patS and ?hetN. Indeed, the EMD values between the WT and all the mutants, displayed in the panels corresponding to 24 hours, confirm this.
abstract_sentence: PatS and HetN differ as HetR inhibitors in timing and role during heterocyst pattern formation; septal proteins SepJ and FraC/FraD differ in specificity affecting cell-cell communication.

fact: Proteins involved in activation, inhibition, and cell-cell communication combine with inevitable stochasticity in gene expression to control coupled fluctuations that give rise to a one-dimensional developmental pattern in Anabaena.
source_span: Our results show that proteins involved in these basic ingredients combine together in the presence of inevitable stochasticity in gene expression , to control the coupled fluctuations of gene expression that give rise to a one-dimensional developmental pattern in this organism . We found that key factors known to act during differentiation following nitrogen deprivation can also play a role before differentiation has been triggered , setting an underlying pattern of spatial correlations of gene expression along filaments , on which the developmental pattern may later be built . In an organism with no specific limit to the number of its cells and on which morphogen gradient fields are not imposed from the outside such as in Drosophila, a developmental pattern can arise from fluctuations in gene expression and activation-inhibition mechanisms such as originally envisioned by Turing.
abstract_sentence: Proteins involved in activation, inhibition, and cell-cell communication combine with stochastic gene expression to control coupled fluctuations that generate the one-dimensional developmental pattern in Anabaena filaments.

fact: Humans can learn and store multiple visuomotor mappings when feedback for each mapping is provided alternately.
source_span: Humans can learn and store multiple visuomotor mappings ( dual-adaptation ) when feedback for each is provided alternately .
abstract_sentence: Humans can learn and store multiple visuomotor mappings when feedback for each is provided alternately.

fact: Learned context cues associated with each visuomotor mapping can be used to switch between the stored mappings.
source_span: Moreover , learned context cues associated with each mapping can be used to switch between the stored mappings . When , after training , either of these target colours is presented , we immediately switch to the correct mapping without the need for feedback to correct our movements .
abstract_sentence: Learned context cues associated with each visuomotor mapping can be used to switch between the stored mappings.

fact: Little is known about the associative learning between cue and required visuomotor mapping, and how learning generalises to novel but similar conditions.
source_span: However , little is known about the associative learning between cue and required visuomotor mapping , and how learning generalises to novel but similar conditions . It is important to note , however , that in most of these studies the role of the learned associations was investigated for only two discrete association-stimulus/visuomotor-mapping pairings . That is , in many of these studies , the context cue could often only have one of two discrete states: the presence or absence of the cue . In this case , testing conditions cannot go beyond the specifically trained pairings to see how the trained pairings generalise to novel conditions ( a cue cannot be half present ) . However , many cues , like the location of targets when learning the distortions for a single pair of glasses , can vary in a continuous manner . The question arises how learning for a discrete number of trained pairings affects the learning rate and generalises to novel conditions on the same continuous cue scale .
abstract_sentence: Little is known about how associative learning between cues and required visuomotor mappings generalises to novel but similar conditions.

fact: To investigate these questions, participants performed a rapid target-pointing task while we manipulated the offset between visual feedback and movement end-points. The visual feedback was presented with horizontal offsets of different amounts, dependent on the targets shape.
source_span: To investigate these questions , participants performed a rapid target-pointing task while we manipulated the offset between visual feedback and movement end-points . The visual feedback was presented with horizontal offsets of different amounts , dependent on the targets shape .
abstract_sentence: Participants performed a rapid target-pointing task with visual feedback offsets dependent on target shape to study visuomotor mapping learning.

fact: The target shapes were taken from a continuous set of shapes, morphed between spiky and circular shapes.
source_span: The target shapes were taken from a continuous set of shapes , morphed between spiky and circular shapes . In the present study we circumvented these problems by investigating how learning and generalisation occurs for associations with a task-irrelevant property of the target in a rapid pointing task. Here, we chose target shape as the contextual cue that ranged from circular to spiky on a continuous scale. Participants performed a target-pointing task in which we manipulated the spatial mapping of the visual feedback that participants received upon completion of their pointing movements ... We generated different target shapes using a morphing method. Shapes ranged from very spiky to completely round. In the first experiment, participants were trained on two specific target shape/mapping contingencies along this continuous scale. One training combination was a shape with ? = 0.125 (a relatively spiky shape) and a mapping of ??5 mm ... the other training combination was shape ? = 0.875 (almost circular) and a mapping of +75 mm.
abstract_sentence: Target shapes were morphed continuously between spiky and circular shapes to create a continuous cue for visuomotor mapping.

fact: After training we tested participants performance , without feedback , on different target shapes that had not been learned previously.
source_span: After training we tested participants performance , without feedback , on different target shapes that had not been learned previously . Afterwards, using catch trials for which the task-relevant visual feedback was eliminated, we tested participants’ pointing performance to target shapes that had not been used explicitly during training ... we specifically tested participants’ performance on different target shape morphs that could either be in-between the two training shapes along the shape morph axis (interpolation) or that could come from further outside (extrapolation). The other 60 trials were catch trials in which we tested the transfer of training to other target shapes . On catch trials participants did not receive any visual feedback indicating the pointing end-point ...
abstract_sentence: After training, participants were tested without feedback on novel target shapes that had not been learned previously.

fact: Participants apply the mapping corresponding to the trained shape that is most similar to the current one, consistent with the Bayesian learning model.
source_span: participants apply the mapping corresponding to the trained shape that is most similar to the current one , consistent with the Bayesian learning model . The experimental results show that , although learning the associations requires explicit awareness of the cues??role , Participants who had not noticed the shape-mapping contingency also did not learn to adjust their behaviour differentially corresponding to the target shape. For more spiky shapes the behavioural mapping does not follow the linear extrapolation prediction ... the transfer of learning to extrapolation shapes seems to occur in a way that the mapping for the more extreme shapes is the same as for the nearest trained shape.
abstract_sentence: Participants applied the visuomotor mapping corresponding to the trained shape most similar to the current one, consistent with the Bayesian learning model.

fact: The Bayesian learning model predicts that learning should slow down with increased numbers of training pairs, which was confirmed by the present results.
source_span: Furthermore , the Bayesian learning model predicts that learning should slow down with increased numbers of training pairs , which was confirmed by the present results . In different experiments we varied the number of training pairs (target shape/mapping pairings) to investigate differences due to the amount of information available for extracting the linear rule for generalisation to novel shapes as well as how the number of training pairs affects learning rates. The model therefore predicts a slow down of the overall learning rate with an increased number of shape-mapping pairs to be learned. When multiple pairs need to be learned simultaneously, these will interfere with each other due to the generalisation of local learning. The model therefore predicts a slow down of the overall learning rate with an increased number of shape-mapping pairs to be learned.
abstract_sentence: The Bayesian learning model predicts that learning slows down with increased numbers of training pairs, which was confirmed by the experimental results.

fact: We found a good correspondence between the Bayesian learning model and the empirical results indicating that this model poses a possible mechanism for simultaneously learning multiple visuomotor mappings.
source_span: In short , we found a good correspondence between the Bayesian learning model and the empirical results indicating that this model poses a possible mechanism for simultaneously learning multiple visuomotor mappings . This is first evidence that the 5 shape-mapping contingencies are learned independently ( as predicted by the Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters ) and it is not the linear relationship that is learned. We used the approach of Bayes-optimal learning ... Here we modelled the learning of the shape-mapping contingencies as a Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters in which each shape is coupled to its own Kalman Filter . Here we modelled the learning of the shape-mapping contingencies as a Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters in which each shape is coupled to its own Kalman Filter.
abstract_sentence: The Bayesian learning model provides a possible mechanism for simultaneously learning multiple visuomotor mappings.

fact: Currently, each NTD program has its own methodology. Conducting multiple surveys in the same country can be costly and burdensome to national disease programs.
source_span: Currently , each NTD program has its own methodology [8] . Conducting multiple surveys in the same country can be costly and burdensome to national disease programs .
abstract_sentence: Each neglected tropical disease (NTD) program currently uses its own mapping methodology, which can be costly and burdensome when multiple surveys are needed.

fact: Because NTDs tend to overlap in geographic areas, it is logical that an integrated approach to mapping NTDs might result in more efficient identification of populations needing treatment.
source_span: Because NTDs tend to overlap in geographic areas , it is logical that an integrated approach to mapping NTDs might result in more efficient identification of populations needing treatment [9] .
abstract_sentence: Because NTDs tend to overlap geographically, an integrated mapping approach could save resources and improve identification of populations needing treatment.

fact: We developed and field-tested an innovative integrated NTD mapping protocol ( Integrated Threshold Mapping ( ITM ) Methodology ) for lymphatic filariasis ( LF ) , trachoma , schistosomiasis and soil-transmitted helminths ( STH ) .
source_span: We developed and field-tested an innovative integrated NTD mapping protocol ( Integrated Threshold Mapping ( ITM ) Methodology ) for lymphatic filariasis ( LF ) , trachoma , schistosomiasis and soil-transmitted helminths ( STH ) .
abstract_sentence: An innovative integrated NTD mapping protocol called Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) was developed and field-tested for lymphatic filariasis, trachoma, schistosomiasis, and soil-transmitted helminths.

fact: The protocol is designed to be resource-efficient , and its specific purpose is to determine whether a threshold to trigger public health interventions in an implementation unit has been attained .
source_span: The protocol is designed to be resource-efficient , and its specific purpose is to determine whether a threshold to trigger public health interventions in an implementation unit has been attained . We describe an integrated NTD mapping methodology ( Integrated Threshold Mapping ) that can be used as an operational tool by Ministries of Health in NTD-endemic countries to determine if the threshold needed to launch disease-specific public health intervenions has been reached .
abstract_sentence: The ITM protocol is designed to be resource-efficient and determines whether a disease threshold to trigger public health interventions has been reached in an implementation unit.

fact: The protocol relies on World Health Organization ( WHO ) recommended indicators in the disease-specific age groups . For each disease , the sampling frame was the district , but for schistosomiasis , the sub-district rather than the ecological zone was used .
source_span: The protocol relies on World Health Organization ( WHO ) recommended indicators in the disease-specific age groups . For each disease , the sampling frame was the district , but for schistosomiasis , the sub-district rather than the ecological zone was used .
abstract_sentence: The ITM protocol uses WHO-recommended disease indicators and age groups, with the district as the sampling frame except for schistosomiasis where the sub-district is used.

fact: We tested the protocol by comparing it to current WHO mapping methodologies for each of the targeted diseases in one district each in Mali and Senegal .
source_span: We tested the protocol by comparing it to current WHO mapping methodologies for each of the targeted diseases in one district each in Mali and Senegal .
abstract_sentence: The ITM protocol was field-tested by comparing it to WHO mapping methodologies in one district each in Mali and Senegal.

fact: In this study , the ITM methodology reached the same conclusions as the WHO methodologies regarding the initiation of public health interventions for trachoma , LF and STH , but resulted in more targeted intervention recommendations for schistosomiasis .
source_span: In this study , the ITM methodology reached the same conclusions as the WHO methodologies regarding the initiation of public health interventions for trachoma , LF and STH , but resulted in more targeted intervention recommendations for schistosomiasis .
abstract_sentence: The ITM methodology agreed with WHO methods on public health interventions for trachoma, lymphatic filariasis, and soil-transmitted helminths, but gave more targeted recommendations for schistosomiasis.

fact: ITM was practical , feasible and demonstrated an overall cost saving compared with the standard , non-integrated , WHO methodologies .
source_span: ITM was practical , feasible and demonstrated an overall cost saving compared with the standard , non-integrated , WHO methodologies . The results of the cost data analysis Table 4 , indicate that using the ITM methodology resulted in a 31% overall cost savings in Mali ( $6 , 968 vs . $10 , 039 ) , and a 19% overall cost savings in Senegal ( $8 , 442 vs . $10 , 372 ) . The integrated approach proved to be more efficient in cost , transport , time in the field and the use of human resources . The ITM methodology used one vehicle to transport the team , versus 3 used in the WHO methodologies , employed a 5-member team instead of a 7-member team , and took about half as much time to implement as the WHO methodologies .
abstract_sentence: The ITM methodology was practical, feasible, and demonstrated overall cost savings compared with standard WHO methodologies.

fact: This integrated mapping tool could facilitate the implementation of much-needed programs in endemic countries .
source_span: This integrated mapping tool could facilitate the implementation of much-needed programs in endemic countries .
abstract_sentence: This integrated mapping tool could facilitate implementation of much-needed NTD programs in endemic countries.
